Scope:

The line above names the paths this work is allowed to touch, at column zero,
before anything else. One path or several.

The contribution guide asks an issue for three things, and they are the three
headings below. An issue that answers all three can be picked up by somebody who
was not in the conversation that produced it.

## What is wrong

The problem, stated as a problem rather than as the absence of your solution.

## What the evidence is

Where the evidence is a number, it carries the command that produced it, run
against the reference a reader will have rather than against your working tree.

Where a claim cannot be backed by a command, write it as a claim. "Verified",
"not measured" and "not evaluated" are three different statements and this
section should say which one it is.

## What done means

A list somebody else can check. Each entry is a thing that will be true
afterwards and is not true now, rather than a task that will have been performed.

A negative disclosure stays negative: if this issue admits something was not
done, that admission survives every later edit.
